summary: Gerald R. Ford International Airport (GRR) is the principal commercial airport serving Grand Rapids and western Michigan, renamed in 1987 in honor of Gerald R. Ford, the 38th U.S. President who grew up in Grand Rapids. Located about 13 miles southeast of downtown Grand Rapids, it is the second-busiest airport in Michigan by passenger volume. The airport serves as a key hub for business travel and offers nonstop service to numerous domestic destinations.
faqs:
Q: How far is Gerald R. Ford International Airport from downtown Grand Rapids?
A: The airport is approximately 13 miles southeast of downtown Grand Rapids, typically a 20-25 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Does GRR offer nonstop international flights?
A: The airport primarily offers domestic service; international connections typically require a stop at a larger hub such as Chicago O'Hare or Detroit.

Q: What airlines operate at Gerald R. Ford International Airport?
A: Major carriers serving GRR include Delta Air Lines, American Airlines, United Airlines, Southwest Airlines, Alaska Airlines, Allegiant Air, and Frontier Airlines.

Q: Is there a military or presidential connection to this airport?
A: The airport is named after Gerald R. Ford, the 38th President of the United States, who was raised in Grand Rapids. A bronze statue of President Ford is displayed in the terminal.
transport_tips: The Rapid bus system (Route 17) provides affordable public transit between the airport and downtown Grand Rapids. Rideshare services like Uber and Lyft, as well as rental car facilities, are available on-site. Taxis and hotel shuttles are also accessible from the terminal's designated pickup areas.
local_tip: If you have time before your flight, stop by the Ford Presidential Museum in downtown Grand Rapids, which offers free admission and a fascinating look at the only president from Michigan.
